_comment: The pause menu, described rather than coded. The previous prototype kept its menu in src/data/pauseMenu.json for the same reason: adding a screen should be a JSON entry plus a tab script, never a new branch in the shell.
_comment_tabs: Order is the on-screen order. `script` is the tab body; it must extend scripts/ui/menu_tab.gd. tests/test_menu_config.gd fails the build if a listed script is missing, because a typo'd path would otherwise show as a silently blank tab.
_comment_open: `menu_cancel` is Escape / B by DEFAULT and the player can now move it — Settings > Controls. It shares its default with `combat_run`, so out of the box the menu still refuses to open mid-fight; see docs/decisions/D14. `inventory` (I / Y) opens straight onto the backpack and works everywhere the menu does.
_comment_cycle: `tool_cycle` (Q / left shoulder) steps to the next tab. Shoulder buttons are the handheld convention for this. The tab row is also focusable, and left/right on it does the same job.
_comment_backpack: `columns` x rows must equal autoload/inventory.gd's SLOT_COUNT, which tests/test_menu_config.gd checks. `hotbar_columns` is where the quick-select band ends; GAME_DESIGN.md 19 wants quick tool selection and this is the row it will live on.
_comment_settings: The settings screen, section by section. `sections` is the running order; today it holds Controls alone. Display and audio are entries here plus a builder in scripts/ui/tab_settings.gd when someone actually writes them — the tab already loops this list, so neither is a rewrite.
_comment_controls: `groups` is what the Controls section draws, in order, and it is the ONLY list of what the player may rebind. Nothing that starts with `ui_` may ever be added: those are Godot's focus navigation, they are what drives this very screen with a stick, and a player who rebound `ui_down` could not reach the control that would undo it. tests/test_controls.gd enforces both that rule and that every action named here is really in the input map.
_comment_glyphs: Button names for an Xbox-layout pad, which is what the ROG Ally is. A PlayStation glyph set is a swap of this block and nothing else. Keys are the stored binding codes from scripts/ui/key_bindings.gd.

groups.name: Looking around
groups.note: The mouse always looks around. That is camera code rather than an input-map action, so it is not listed here and cannot be changed.

_comment_footer: The button legend. Written out because this ships on a handheld with no manual open beside it.
footer: A  Select        B  Close        Q / LB  Next tab
